replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: To solve a second-order algebraic equation: 1) Write it in standard form (ax² + bx + c = 0). 2) Identify coefficients a, b, and c. 3) Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac) to determine solution type. 4) Apply the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a). 5) Simplify each root. If discriminant is negative, solutions are complex numbers involving imaginary unit i.

To find stationary points: 1) Find f'(x), the first derivative of f(x). 2) Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x values. 3) Substitute each x value back into original function to get corresponding y coordinates. 4) Classify each point using second derivative test (f'' > 0 indicates minimum, f'' < 0 indicates maximum, f'' = 0 requires further analysis). These points mark where tangent lines are horizontal.
replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: PCA involves: 1) Standardizing your data if variables have different scales. 2) Computing the correlation matrix. 3) Finding eigenvalues and eigenvectors of this matrix. 4) Sorting eigenvalues in descending order to identify principal components. 5) Selecting top k components that explain most variance. 6) Transforming original data into new coordinate system. Don't worry—while conceptually complex, the core idea is dimensionality reduction while preserving maximum information.
